summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence presented with abdominal bloating/distention and increased, discolored G-tube output while taking metronidazole and norfloxacin at home for suspected recurrent small intestinal bacterial overgrowth. She was admitted to the bariatric surgery service and initially managed with bowel rest (NPO), IV fluids, and IV piperacillin-tazobactam. Abdominal radiography showed a nonobstructive bowel gas pattern without free air, and a contrast G-tube study confirmed a patent tube positioned in the stomach without extraluminal leak. She received soap-suds enemas for distention and was transitioned to IV ceftriaxone plus metronidazole, with restart of tube feeds and advancement to a bariatric Stage V diet, both tolerated without nausea or discomfort. She remained afebrile and clinically improved; blood cultures showed no growth, and stool testing was negative for toxigenic C. difficile and common bacterial pathogens. She was discharged home ambulatory and mentally clear with instructions to continue metronidazole, avoid NSAIDs, remain on Stage V diet, and coordinate tube feed regimen with her bariatric clinic.
